subject: History of India
questionText: The Indus Valley Civilization was primarily:
solution: The Indus Valley (Harappan) Civilization was notable for its advanced urban planning, including grid-pattern streets, drainage systems, and standardized brick sizes.

subject: History of India
questionText: The Ashoka Pillar at Sarnath is associated with:
solution: Sarnath is where Buddha delivered his first sermon (Dhammacakkappavattana Sutta). The Ashoka Pillar with its lion capital was erected here to commemorate this event.

subject: History of India
questionText: Which Vedic text is considered the oldest?
solution: The Rig Veda (c. 1500-1200 BCE) is the oldest of the four Vedas and one of the oldest known texts in any Indo-European language.

subject: History of India
questionText: The Mauryan Empire was founded by:
solution: Chandragupta Maurya founded the Mauryan Empire around 321 BCE with the guidance of his advisor Chanakya (Kautilya). Ashoka was his grandson.

subject: History of India
questionText: The concept of "Dharma Chakra" on the Indian national flag is taken from:
solution: The 24-spoke Dharma Chakra (Wheel of Law) on India's flag is derived from the Ashoka Pillar at Sarnath, which also provides the national emblem.

subject: History of India
questionText: Nalanda University was destroyed by:
solution: Bakhtiyar Khilji destroyed Nalanda University around 1193 CE. The library was so vast that it reportedly burned for three months.

subject: History of India
questionText: The Permanent Settlement of 1793 was introduced by:
solution: Lord Cornwallis introduced the Permanent Settlement in Bengal in 1793, fixing land revenue to be paid by zamindars to the British government permanently.

subject: History of India
questionText: The Doctrine of Lapse was associated with:
solution: Lord Dalhousie used the Doctrine of Lapse to annex Indian states whose rulers died without natural heirs, including Satara, Jhansi, and Nagpur.

subject: Indian National Movement
questionText: The Non-Cooperation Movement was launched in:
solution: Gandhi launched the Non-Cooperation Movement in 1920 against the Rowlatt Act and Jallianwala Bagh massacre. It was suspended in 1922 after the Chauri Chaura incident.

subject: Indian National Movement
questionText: The Salt March (Dandi March) took place in:
solution: Gandhi led the Salt March from Sabarmati Ashram to Dandi (about 390 km) in March-April 1930 to protest the British salt tax, launching the Civil Disobedience Movement.

subject: Indian National Movement
questionText: "Do or Die" was the slogan of which movement?
solution: Gandhi gave the "Do or Die" (Karo ya Maro) call during the Quit India Movement launched on August 8, 1942, demanding an end to British rule.

subject: Indian National Movement
questionText: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre occurred in:
solution: On April 13, 1919, General Dyer ordered troops to fire on a peaceful gathering at Jallianwala Bagh in Amritsar, killing hundreds of unarmed civilians.

subject: Indian National Movement
questionText: Who founded the Indian National Congress in 1885?
solution: Allan Octavian Hume, a retired British civil servant, founded the Indian National Congress in 1885. The first session was held in Bombay under W.C. Bonnerjee.

subject: Indian National Movement
questionText: The Rowlatt Act of 1919 was opposed because it:
solution: The Rowlatt Act allowed the British government to imprison any person suspected of terrorism without trial for up to two years, severely curtailing civil liberties.

subject: Indian and World Geography
questionText: The Tropic of Cancer passes through how many Indian states?
solution: The Tropic of Cancer (23.5°N) passes through 8 Indian states: Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura, and Mizoram.

subject: Indian and World Geography
questionText: Which is the longest river in India?
solution: The Ganga is the longest river in India at approximately 2,525 km. Godavari (1,465 km) is the longest peninsular river.

subject: Indian and World Geography
questionText: The Western Ghats are also known as:
solution: The Western Ghats are also called Sahyadri. They run along the western coast of India for about 1,600 km from Gujarat to Tamil Nadu.

subject: Indian and World Geography
questionText: Which Indian state has the longest coastline?
solution: Gujarat has the longest coastline among Indian states at approximately 1,600 km, followed by Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu.

subject: Indian and World Geography
questionText: The Deccan Plateau is bounded by:
optionC: Western Ghats, Eastern Ghats, and Satpura Range
solution: The Deccan Plateau is a triangular landmass bounded by the Western Ghats (west), Eastern Ghats (east), and the Satpura-Vindhya ranges (north).

subject: Indian and World Geography
questionText: Monsoon winds in India are caused primarily by:
optionB: Differential heating of land and sea
solution: The Indian monsoon is driven by differential heating between the Indian landmass and the Indian Ocean, creating pressure differences that drive seasonal wind patterns.

subject: Indian and World Geography
questionText: The Chilika Lake is located in:
solution: Chilika Lake in Odisha is the largest coastal lagoon in India and the second largest in the world. It is a Ramsar wetland site.

subject: Indian and World Geography
questionText: Which soil type is most suitable for cotton cultivation?
solution: Black soil (Regur/Black Cotton Soil) is ideal for cotton cultivation due to its high moisture retention capacity. It is found mainly in the Deccan Plateau.

subject: Indian Polity and Governance
questionText: The Indian Constitution was adopted on:
solution: The Constitution was adopted on November 26, 1949, and came into effect on January 26, 1950 (Republic Day). August 15, 1947 was Independence Day.

subject: Indian Polity and Governance
questionText: The Preamble of the Indian Constitution begins with:
solution: "We, the people of India" — this phrase establishes popular sovereignty, meaning the Constitution derives its authority from the people of India.

subject: Indian Polity and Governance
questionText: Which article abolishes untouchability?
solution: Article 17 abolishes untouchability and forbids its practice in any form. Enforcement of any disability arising from untouchability is a punishable offence.

subject: Indian Polity and Governance
questionText: The concept of Fundamental Duties was added by which amendment?
solution: The 42nd Amendment (1976) added Fundamental Duties under Article 51A, based on the Swaran Singh Committee recommendations. Originally 10 duties, now 11.

subject: Indian Polity and Governance
questionText: Right to Education is a Fundamental Right under:
solution: Article 21A (added by 86th Amendment, 2002) makes free and compulsory education a Fundamental Right for children aged 6-14 years.

subject: Indian Polity and Governance
questionText: The President of India is elected by:
optionC: An electoral college of elected MPs and MLAs
solution: The President is elected by an electoral college consisting of elected members of both Houses of Parliament and elected members of State Legislative Assemblies (Article 54).

subject: Indian Polity and Governance
questionText: Which Fundamental Right is available only to Indian citizens and not to foreigners?
solution: Article 19 rights (speech, assembly, movement, etc.) are available only to citizens. Articles 14, 21, and 23 are available to all persons including foreigners.

subject: Indian Polity and Governance
questionText: The Right to Property was removed as a Fundamental Right by:
solution: The 44th Amendment (1978) removed Right to Property from Fundamental Rights. It is now a legal right under Article 300A.

subject: Economic and Social Development
questionText: India's GDP is primarily driven by which sector?
solution: The services sector contributes approximately 54% of India's GDP, followed by industry (~26%) and agriculture (~20%).

subject: Economic and Social Development
questionText: The Reserve Bank of India was established in:
solution: RBI was established on April 1, 1935, based on the recommendations of the Hilton Young Commission. It was nationalized in 1949.

subject: Economic and Social Development
questionText: NITI Aayog replaced which body?
solution: NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) replaced the Planning Commission on January 1, 2015, shifting from centralized planning to cooperative federalism.

subject: Economic and Social Development
questionText: GST was implemented in India from:
solution: The Goods and Services Tax (GST) was launched on July 1, 2017, through the 101st Constitutional Amendment, replacing multiple indirect taxes.

subject: Economic and Social Development
questionText: The fiscal deficit of the government refers to:
optionC: Total expenditure minus total receipts excluding borrowings
solution: Fiscal Deficit = Total Expenditure - Total Receipts (excluding borrowings). It indicates the total borrowing requirement of the government.

subject: Economic and Social Development
questionText: Which of the following is NOT a direct tax?
solution: GST is an indirect tax levied on goods and services. Direct taxes (Income Tax, Corporate Tax, Capital Gains Tax) are paid directly by the taxpayer to the government.

subject: Economic and Social Development
questionText: The Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) guarantees:
solution: MGNREGA guarantees 100 days of wage employment per year to every rural household whose adult members volunteer to do unskilled manual work.

subject: Economic and Social Development
questionText: The Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana aims at:
solution: PMJDY (launched 2014) is a financial inclusion program providing universal access to banking facilities with zero-balance accounts, RuPay debit cards, and insurance cover.

subject: Environmental Ecology
questionText: Which of the following is a biodiversity hotspot in India?
solution: India has 4 biodiversity hotspots: Western Ghats, Eastern Himalayas, Indo-Burma, and Sundaland. The Western Ghats host over 5,000 flowering plant species.

subject: Environmental Ecology
questionText: The Kyoto Protocol is related to:
solution: The Kyoto Protocol (1997) is an international treaty committing industrialized nations to reduce greenhouse gas emissions. It was the first binding agreement on climate change.

subject: Environmental Ecology
questionText: The National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC) includes how many missions?
solution: NAPCC (2008) includes 8 missions: Solar, Enhanced Energy Efficiency, Sustainable Habitat, Water, Sustaining Himalayan Ecosystem, Green India, Sustainable Agriculture, and Strategic Knowledge.

subject: Environmental Ecology
questionText: Coral reefs are formed by:
solution: Coral reefs are built by colonies of tiny animals called coral polyps, which secrete calcium carbonate to form hard skeletons. They thrive in warm, shallow, clear waters.

subject: Environmental Ecology
questionText: The Ramsar Convention is related to:
solution: The Ramsar Convention (1971) is an international treaty for the conservation and sustainable use of wetlands. India has over 75 Ramsar sites.

subject: Environmental Ecology
questionText: Which gas is the largest contributor to the greenhouse effect?
solution: Water vapor is the most abundant greenhouse gas and contributes most to the natural greenhouse effect. However, CO2 is the most significant human-caused greenhouse gas.

subject: Environmental Ecology
questionText: Project Tiger was launched in:
solution: Project Tiger was launched on April 1, 1973, to protect the Bengal tiger. Jim Corbett National Park was the first tiger reserve. India now has 50+ tiger reserves.

subject: Environmental Ecology
questionText: The Wildlife Protection Act was enacted in:
solution: The Wildlife Protection Act, 1972, provides for the protection of wild animals, birds, and plants. It established the framework for wildlife sanctuaries and national parks.

subject: General Science
questionText: The SI unit of force is:
solution: The Newton (N) is the SI unit of force. 1 Newton = force needed to accelerate 1 kg mass by 1 m/s². Named after Sir Isaac Newton.

subject: General Science
questionText: Which phenomenon explains why the sky appears blue?
solution: Rayleigh scattering causes shorter wavelengths (blue/violet) to scatter more than longer wavelengths. Our eyes are more sensitive to blue, making the sky appear blue.

subject: General Science
questionText: A concave mirror is used in:
solution: Concave mirrors converge light and are used in headlights, searchlights, and solar concentrators. Convex mirrors (diverging) are used in rear-view mirrors.

subject: General Science
questionText: DNA stands for:
solution: DNA (Deoxyribonucleic Acid) is the molecule that carries genetic instructions for development, functioning, growth, and reproduction of all known organisms.

subject: General Science
questionText: Photosynthesis primarily occurs in:
solution: Photosynthesis primarily occurs in leaves, specifically in chloroplasts containing chlorophyll. The process converts CO2 and water into glucose and oxygen using sunlight.

subject: General Science
questionText: Which vitamin deficiency causes scurvy?
solution: Scurvy is caused by Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) deficiency. Symptoms include bleeding gums, weakness, and poor wound healing. Found in citrus fruits and vegetables.

subject: General Science
questionText: The pH of pure water is:
solution: Pure water has a pH of 7, which is neutral. pH < 7 is acidic, pH > 7 is basic/alkaline. The pH scale ranges from 0 to 14.

subject: General Science
questionText: Which gas is used in fire extinguishers?
solution: CO2 is used in fire extinguishers because it is heavier than air, does not support combustion, and smothers the fire by displacing oxygen.

subject: Current Events
questionText: The G20 presidency was held by India in:
solution: India held the G20 presidency from December 1, 2022 to November 30, 2023, with the theme "One Earth, One Family, One Future." The summit was held in New Delhi.

subject: Current Events
questionText: The Chandrayaan-3 mission successfully landed on the Moon in:
solution: Chandrayaan-3 successfully soft-landed on the Moon's south pole on August 23, 2023, making India the fourth country to land on the Moon and the first to land near the south pole.

subject: Current Events
questionText: The Aditya-L1 mission is related to:
solution: Aditya-L1 is India's first space-based solar observatory, launched in September 2023. It studies the Sun from the Lagrange point 1 (L1), about 1.5 million km from Earth.

subject: Current Events
questionText: The Uniform Civil Code debate in India relates to:
optionB: Common personal laws for all citizens
solution: The Uniform Civil Code (Article 44, Directive Principles) envisions common personal laws (marriage, divorce, inheritance) for all citizens regardless of religion.

subject: Current Events
questionText: Digital India initiative was launched in:
solution: Digital India was launched on July 1, 2015, to transform India into a digitally empowered society with focus on digital infrastructure, governance, and digital literacy.

subject: Current Events
questionText: The Swachh Bharat Mission was launched on:
solution: Swachh Bharat Mission was launched on October 2, 2014 (Gandhi Jayanti) to achieve universal sanitation coverage and eliminate open defecation by 2019.

subject: History of India
questionText: The Ajanta Caves are famous for:
solution: The Ajanta Caves (2nd century BCE to 6th century CE) in Maharashtra contain masterpieces of Buddhist religious art, including paintings and rock-cut sculptures.

subject: History of India
questionText: Bharatanatyam is a classical dance form originating from:
solution: Bharatanatyam originated in Tamil Nadu and is one of the oldest classical dance forms of India, traditionally performed in Hindu temples.

subject: History of India
questionText: The Konark Sun Temple was built by:
solution: The Konark Sun Temple in Odisha was built by King Narasimhadeva I of the Eastern Ganga dynasty around 1250 CE. It is designed as a giant chariot of the Sun God.

subject: History of India
questionText: Which Mughal emperor built the Taj Mahal?
solution: Shah Jahan built the Taj Mahal (1632-1653) in Agra as a mausoleum for his wife Mumtaz Mahal. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

subject: History of India
questionText: Kathakali is a classical dance-drama from:
solution: Kathakali originated in Kerala in the 17th century. It combines dance, music, and acting, with elaborate costumes and makeup depicting stories from epics.

subject: Indian National Movement
questionText: Bhagat Singh, Rajguru, and Sukhdev were executed on:
solution: Bhagat Singh, Rajguru, and Sukhdev were hanged on March 23, 1931, in Lahore Central Jail for the murder of British police officer J.P. Saunders.

subject: Indian National Movement
questionText: The Hindustan Socialist Republican Association was founded by:
solution: HSRA was founded in 1928 by Chandrashekhar Azad, reorganizing the earlier Hindustan Republican Association (founded by Bismil and others). Bhagat Singh was a key member.

subject: Indian National Movement
questionText: The Kakori Train Robbery of 1925 was organized by:
solution: The Kakori conspiracy (August 9, 1925) was organized by HRA members including Ram Prasad Bismil and Ashfaqulla Khan to fund revolutionary activities.

subject: Indian National Movement
questionText: Subhas Chandra Bose founded the Indian National Army with support from:
solution: Bose reorganized the Indian National Army (Azad Hind Fauj) in 1943 with Japanese support to fight against British rule in India during World War II.

subject: Indian National Movement
questionText: The famous slogan "Inquilab Zindabad" was popularized by:
solution: Bhagat Singh popularized "Inquilab Zindabad" (Long Live the Revolution) as a rallying cry for the Indian independence movement.

subject: Indian Polity and Governance
questionText: The Rajya Sabha can have a maximum of how many members?
solution: Rajya Sabha can have a maximum of 250 members — 238 elected by state and UT legislatures, and 12 nominated by the President for expertise in literature, science, art, and social service.

subject: Indian Polity and Governance
questionText: The Chief Justice of India is appointed by:
solution: The President appoints the CJI, conventionally based on seniority among Supreme Court judges. The collegium system recommends appointments.

subject: Indian Polity and Governance
questionText: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment deals with:
solution: The 73rd Amendment (1992) constitutionalized Panchayati Raj institutions, providing a three-tier system of local self-governance in rural areas.

subject: Indian Polity and Governance
questionText: Money Bills can be introduced in:
solution: Under Article 109, Money Bills can only be introduced in Lok Sabha. Rajya Sabha can suggest amendments within 14 days but Lok Sabha may accept or reject them.

subject: Indian Polity and Governance
questionText: The concept of Judicial Review in India is based on:
solution: Judicial Review derives from multiple articles: Art. 13 (laws inconsistent with Fundamental Rights are void), Art. 32 (Supreme Court writs), and Art. 226 (High Court writs).

subject: Economic and Social Development
questionText: India's Human Development Index (HDI) is published by:
solution: The HDI is published annually by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP). It measures life expectancy, education, and per capita income.

subject: Economic and Social Development
questionText: The Right to Information Act was enacted in:
solution: The RTI Act was enacted on June 15, 2005, replacing the Freedom of Information Act, 2002. It empowers citizens to seek information from public authorities.

subject: Economic and Social Development
questionText: The National Food Security Act guarantees:
optionB: Subsidized food grains to about 2/3 of the population
solution: The NFSA (2013) provides subsidized food grains (rice at ₹3/kg, wheat at ₹2/kg, coarse grains at ₹1/kg) to approximately 75% rural and 50% urban population.

subject: Economic and Social Development
questionText: The Beti Bachao Beti Padhao scheme addresses:
optionB: Declining child sex ratio and girls' education
solution: Launched in 2015, Beti Bachao Beti Padhao addresses the declining Child Sex Ratio and promotes education and empowerment of the girl child.

subject: Economic and Social Development
questionText: The Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act was enacted in:
solution: The SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, was enacted to prevent atrocities and discrimination against Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.

subject: General Science
questionText: 5G technology primarily operates in which frequency bands?
optionB: Sub-6 GHz and millimeter wave (24-100 GHz)
solution: 5G uses sub-6 GHz bands for coverage and millimeter wave (mmWave) bands (24-100 GHz) for high-speed, low-latency applications.

subject: General Science
questionText: Blockchain technology is best described as:
solution: Blockchain is a distributed ledger technology where transactions are recorded in blocks linked cryptographically, making them immutable and transparent.

subject: General Science
questionText: ISRO's PSLV stands for:
solution: PSLV (Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle) is ISRO's workhorse rocket, primarily used to launch satellites into polar and sun-synchronous orbits.

subject: General Science
questionText: Quantum computing differs from classical computing because it uses:
optionB: Qubits that can exist in superposition
solution: Quantum computers use qubits that can exist in superposition (both 0 and 1 simultaneously) and can be entangled, enabling exponentially faster computation for certain problems.

subject: General Science
questionText: The UPI (Unified Payments Interface) was developed by:
solution: UPI was developed by NPCI and launched in 2016. It enables instant real-time inter-bank transactions through mobile phones.

subject: Indian and World Geography
questionText: The Amazon Rainforest is primarily located in:
solution: The Amazon Rainforest covers about 5.5 million km² primarily in Brazil, with portions in Peru, Colombia, and other South American countries. It is the world's largest tropical rainforest.

subject: Indian and World Geography
questionText: The Ring of Fire is associated with:
optionA: Volcanic and seismic activity around the Pacific Ocean
solution: The Ring of Fire is a horseshoe-shaped zone around the Pacific Ocean where about 75% of the world's volcanoes are found and 90% of earthquakes occur.

subject: Indian and World Geography
questionText: The Sahara Desert is located in:
solution: The Sahara is the world's largest hot desert, covering about 9.2 million km² across North Africa, spanning 11 countries.

subject: Indian and World Geography
questionText: The Strait of Malacca connects:
solution: The Strait of Malacca, between the Malay Peninsula and Sumatra, connects the Indian Ocean to the Pacific Ocean. It is one of the world's most important shipping lanes.

subject: Indian and World Geography
questionText: Which continent has the most countries?
solution: Africa has 54 recognized sovereign countries, the most of any continent. Asia has 48, Europe has 44.

subject: Current Events
questionText: The United Nations was established in:
solution: The United Nations was established on October 24, 1945, after World War II. It replaced the League of Nations and currently has 193 member states.

subject: Current Events
questionText: The Paris Agreement on climate change was adopted in:
solution: The Paris Agreement was adopted on December 12, 2015, at COP21. It aims to limit global warming to well below 2°C, preferably 1.5°C, above pre-industrial levels.

subject: Current Events
questionText: BRICS originally consisted of which countries?
optionB: Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa
solution: BRIC was coined in 2001 for Brazil, Russia, India, China. South Africa joined in 2010, making it BRICS. The group expanded further in 2024.

subject: Current Events
questionText: The International Court of Justice is located in:
solution: The ICJ (principal judicial organ of the UN) is located at the Peace Palace in The Hague, Netherlands. It settles disputes between states.

subject: Current Events
questionText: The World Trade Organization was established in:
solution: The WTO was established on January 1, 1995, replacing GATT (General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade). It regulates international trade between nations.

subject: Environmental Ecology
questionText: The ozone layer is primarily found in which layer of the atmosphere?
solution: The ozone layer is located in the stratosphere, approximately 15-35 km above Earth's surface. It absorbs most of the Sun's harmful ultraviolet radiation.

subject: Environmental Ecology
questionText: COP stands for:
solution: COP (Conference of the Parties) is the supreme decision-making body of the UNFCCC. COP meetings are held annually to assess progress on climate change.

subject: Environmental Ecology
questionText: The Montreal Protocol deals with:
solution: The Montreal Protocol (1987) is an international treaty to protect the ozone layer by phasing out ozone-depleting substances like CFCs. It is considered the most successful environmental treaty.

subject: Environmental Ecology
questionText: Which of the following is a greenhouse gas?
solution: Methane (CH4) is a potent greenhouse gas, about 80 times more effective at trapping heat than CO2 over 20 years. Sources include livestock, rice paddies, and fossil fuels.

subject: Environmental Ecology
questionText: The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) was established in:
solution: The IPCC was established in 1988 by the WMO and UNEP to provide scientific assessments on climate change. It shared the Nobel Peace Prize in 2007.
